steps.label: open the Meshes tab
steps.goal: on a blank kit there is nothing to build with yet, so the first job is turning raw meshes into pieces the library knows. Nothing else can happen before this
do: press 2
steps.recovery: if a text field has the keyboard the number types into it: press Escape first

steps.label: find something flat and square for a floor
steps.goal: the floor is what gives a tile its size and its edges, so it is the first piece every kit needs. Shape is what matters here, not the name -- you are looking for a slab
do: press F and type part of a mesh name to filter, then Enter to hand the keyboard back
walk the list with up and down -- packs fold, right opens one
stop on something flat and roughly square
steps.recovery: if the list is empty the filter is hiding everything: press F, Backspace it clear, Enter. If you cannot tell a mesh's shape from the row, say so -- that is the report

steps.label: let the labeller describe it, then check what it said
steps.goal: L asks the vision model what the mesh is and stages a suggestion; U applies it. Staged, not written -- the answer is a proposal until you accept it, because the model is often confidently wrong about mounts
do: press L and wait for the suggestion
read what it proposes
press U to apply it, or Y to throw it away and describe it yourself
steps.recovery: if L reports the model is unreachable, the ssh forward is down -- the message prints the exact command. If the suggestion is wrong, that IS the report: say which field and what it should have been

steps.label: import it into the library
steps.goal: a labelled candidate is still not a piece until it is accepted -- this is the step that puts it in the palette everything else draws from
do: press Enter
steps.recovery: if it refuses, the message names what it objected to -- usually a missing measurement. That message is the report

steps.label: do the same for a wall and a doorway
steps.goal: three pieces is the whole vocabulary a room needs: something to stand on, something to enclose it, and something to walk through. A doorway mesh is a wall with a hole already in it
do: find a tall flat mesh for the wall -- label it, press Enter
find one with an opening in it for the door -- label it, press Enter
press right to look at the IN LIBRARY list and check all three are there
steps.recovery: if you cannot find a doorway mesh, say so and use a second wall for now -- the room will be sealed, which is itself worth seeing

steps.label: open the Tiles tab and start the corner
steps.goal: now the tiles. A corner is where two solid sides meet -- without one a kit can only make corridors, because there is no way to close a room off
do: press 2
press N for a new tile
type a name like corner
press Enter
steps.recovery: if the list on this tab is empty, the meshes did not import -- go back to 2 and check the IN LIBRARY side

steps.label: floor it, then stand two walls at right angles
steps.goal: the floor goes in first because it gives the tile its size. The second wall needs R to turn it a quarter before it can sit flush against the NEXT side round -- that quarter turn is the whole difference between a corner and a doubled wall
do: walk to your floor piece and press Enter
press Escape, walk to your wall piece, press Enter, shift-arrow it flush to one side
press Enter for a second wall, press R to turn it, shift-arrow it flush to an ADJACENT side
steps.recovery: if the second wall will not sit flush it is probably not turned -- press R again. If the arrows walk the list instead of the piece, press Escape then Enter

steps.label: does it read as a corner
steps.goal: before saving: the two walls should meet, not overlap and not leave a gap at the join. This is the question no checkpoint can answer and the reason a person is doing this
do: orbit the camera and look at where the two walls meet
steps.recovery: if they overlap or gap, say which, and say what flush landed on

steps.label: save the corner
steps.goal: saving is what puts it in the kit, and only what is in the kit can be stamped onto a map
do: press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: if it refuses, the message names what it objected to -- that message is the report

steps.label: make the wall tile and the door tile the same way
steps.goal: a plain run, and a run with the doorway in it. Flush the doorway to the SAME side you flushed the wall to -- if the two sit differently, swapping a door into a wall run will not line up, and that misalignment is the likeliest thing this exercise will find
do: press N, name it, floor plus one wall flushed to a side, Cmd+S
press N, name it, floor plus the doorway flushed to the SAME side, Cmd+S
steps.recovery: if a tile will not save, say what it said -- a tile that cannot be saved is a tile that cannot be placed

steps.label: arm the wall tile on the Compose tab
steps.goal: the Map stamps whatever is armed here. This is the step that connects the two halves, and the one an author is least likely to guess
do: press 4
walk to your wall tile with up and down
press Enter to arm it
steps.recovery: the status line says which tile is armed -- if it says nothing was armed, the selection is on something else

steps.label: lay the four walls
steps.goal: now the room. Four runs for the sides -- leave the corners for the next step, and leave one gap in a side for the door
do: press 1 for the Map tab
click to stamp the armed tile
press R or T to turn each one so its solid side faces outward
lay four runs, leaving the corners open and one gap for the door
steps.checkpoint: the map has tiles on it
steps.recovery: if a click places nothing, nothing is armed -- back to 4 and press Enter on the tile

steps.label: close the four corners
steps.goal: the corner tile is what the whole first half was for. Each of the four needs a different quarter turn
do: press 4, walk to the corner tile, press Enter to arm it
press 1
stamp one into each corner, pressing R to turn it to face the right way
steps.checkpoint: the map has tiles on it
steps.recovery: refusing to overlap is correct; landing somewhere you did not point is not. Say which happened

steps.label: put the door in
steps.goal: the last piece, into the gap you left
do: press 4, walk to the door tile, press Enter to arm it
press 1
stamp it into the gap, turned to match the run it sits in
steps.checkpoint: the map has tiles on it
steps.recovery: if it will not go in the gap, the gap is the wrong size -- say what it refused with

steps.label: walk round it and say whether it is a room
steps.goal: the question the whole exercise is for. Not whether the checkpoints passed -- whether what is on screen reads as a room somebody could stand in, built out of meshes that were raw files an hour ago
do: orbit the camera all the way round
look along each run for seams, gaps and doubled-up pieces
look at the doorway: is the hole where a person would walk through it
steps.recovery: everything that looks wrong is the report, however small -- a seam at one corner and not the others is more useful than a general impression

steps.label: save the map
steps.goal: what you built is on disk as nine tile references rather than a hundred loose pieces, in a form the game reads
do: press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: if it refuses, the message names what it objected to
